affected_docs.why: THIS TASK'S PAGE, the only one to edit. Four edit sites, of which two are defects and two are not. (1) Lines 76-78 state that on an 8 GB machine the persona will think and speak one at a time. That is the planner's !coexist warning string (crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:144-148) and an 8 GB Apple Silicon Mac does not reach that branch, so the sentence is contradicted by source and by the pinned test at crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:36-52; lines 39-42 in the same page are correct. (2) Lines 85-86 state the Windows default install root is `D:\Hearth`. crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:232-251 names no drive letter: on Windows it is `Hearth` on the roomiest non-removable non-system fixed drive, falling back to `%USERPROFILE%\Hearth` on a single-drive machine; the macOS half of the sentence is correct. (3) Lines 96-97 name four things downloading beside a plan figure that counts two of them; the sentence is accurate about what provisioning does (desktop-client/src-tauri/src/provision.rs:1-14, desktop-client/src/lib/probe.ts:120-134) but the number the page prints at line 72 covers only the model weights and the OmniVoice weights (crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:214-234). (4) The four figures at lines 42-44, 72 and 75 are NOT stale: 3.77 GB, 7.14 GB, 4.5 GB and 8.6 GB each reproduce a planner quantity under the product's own renderer, so they need no arithmetic change. One further defect sits inside the same `## The download` section: line 100's `Every file is verified against a published sha256 hash once it lands` is contradicted for the voice weights and the inference engine, which carry no hash.

claims.claim: wiki/installing.md states, of the same machine, both that an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air runs the mind and the voice at once and that on an 8 GB machine the persona will think and speak one at a time.

claims.claim: An 8 GB Apple Silicon Mac plans with the mind and the voice both resident, so lines 39-42 are the correct half of the contradiction.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:104-136. Pool for the m1-air-8gb fixture is ram_bytes, 8,589,934,592 (machine.rs:297-314, vram None so memory_pool falls to RAM at machine.rs:52-57). base = stt 805,306,368 + headroom 1,073,741,824 + os_unified 2,415,919,104 = 4,294,967,296 (dictionary.yaml:79-89, plan.rs:110-113). macOS is in cpp_platforms (dictionary.yaml:102) so voice_resident is 966,367,641 (dictionary.yaml:113, dict.rs:76-78). coexist_budget = 3,328,599,655, which holds tier 0 Q4_K_M at 3,106,738,272 (dictionary.yaml:162-165) with room for context, so best_fit succeeds on the coexist branch at plan.rs:128-136 and coexist is true. Pinned as a contract at crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:36-52, which asserts p.coexist and asserts that no warning contains `one at a time`.

claims.claim: wiki/installing.md:76-78 is contradicted: the take-turns phrasing is the planner's warning for the !coexist branch, which an 8 GB Mac does not reach.
claims.evidence: The page states it at wiki/installing.md:75-79. The opposite is stated by crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:137-150, where the warning `Your persona will think and speak one at a time` is pushed only inside the sequential-budget branch, and by crates/hearth-probe/tests/plan_fixtures.rs:48-51, whose comment records that this test used to assert the opposite and changed when omnivoice.cpp replaced the torch voice.

claims.claim: On macOS the !coexist branch is unreachable for any machine Hearth accepts, so no Mac produces the take-turns warning.
claims.evidence: Derived from crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:110-159 with dictionary.yaml:79-89, 102, 113, 162-177. On unified memory the held-back base plus the C++ voice is a fixed 5,261,334,937 bytes. At 8 GB the remaining 3,328,599,655 already clears tier 0 Q4_K_M plus a context floor (3,157,069,920), and every larger Mac clears it by more; at 6 GB the sequential budget of 2,147,483,648 is below the smallest build plus floor (2,587,117,664) and plan.rs:151-157 refuses the machine outright. The band between refusal and coexistence is not a size any Apple Silicon Mac ships in. Arithmetic mine, from cited constants; not executed.

claims.claim: The !coexist branch is nonetheless live code and is reached by a machine with roughly 4.5 to 5.4 GB of dedicated VRAM.
claims.evidence: Derived from crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:110-159 with dictionary.yaml:79-89, 102, 113, 174-177. On a non-unified machine base is 1,879,048,192 and the C++ voice 966,367,641, so coexistence needs a pool above about 5.43 GB while a plan of any kind needs a pool above about 4.47 GB. A 5 GB card (5,368,709,120) has a coexist budget of 2,523,293,287, under the 2,587,117,664 the smallest build plus its context floor needs, and a sequential budget of 3,489,660,928, which holds tier 0 Q4_K_M. No fixture exercises this and it is not a Mac; recorded because it is what an honest replacement sentence at lines 76-78 can still say about a small machine. Arithmetic mine, from cited constants; not executed.

claims.claim: An 8 GB Mac plans an n_ctx of 17,408, so the figure at wiki/installing.md:71 is correct.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:163 and ctx_for at 279-283. left = 3,328,599,655 - 3,106,738,272 = 221,861,383 bytes; divided by tier 0's kv_bytes_per_token of 12,288 (dictionary.yaml:141) that is 18,054 raw, clamped under max_ctx 32,768 (dictionary.yaml:140) and rounded down to a multiple of 1024 by plan.rs:282, giving 17,408. Cross-check on the method: the same constants render the planner's reason string at plan.rs:187-190 as `212 MB is left after the weights, which is about 17408 tokens of context at this model's rate`, because 221,861,383 bytes is 211.58 MiB and human() formats sub-GiB values to a whole MiB (crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:26-34). That is the string the dispatching lead reported from an executed run, reproduced here from source alone.

claims.claim: The plan table's model row for an 8 GB Mac, Gemma 4 E2B at Q4_K_M, is what the planner chooses.
claims.evidence: dictionary.yaml:134 names the model and 161-165 puts Q4_K_M first on the ladder; plan.rs:161-163 takes ladder[0] when it fits, and fit_at at plan.rs:308-321 accepts it because its 17,408-token window clears TARGET_CTX 16,384 (plan.rs:25, 299). Asserted at crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:337-344.

claims.claim: A 16 GB Mac plans Gemma 4 12B at a 65,536-token window, so wiki/installing.md:74-75 is correct on both counts.
claims.evidence: machine.rs:315-332 gives the m1-air-16gb fixture 17,179,869,184 bytes of RAM, so coexist_budget is 11,918,534,247. Tier 2's weights are 6,716,356,800 (dictionary.yaml:204), leaving 5,202,177,447 over a kv rate of 57,344 (dictionary.yaml:207), which is 90,718 raw and clamps to max_ctx 65,536 (dictionary.yaml:206) at plan.rs:282. claims.claim: The free-disk figures at wiki/installing.md:42-44 name disk_required_bytes, and 4.5 GB and 8.6 GB are that quantity rendered and rounded to one decimal.
claims.evidence: disk_required = total + total/5 at crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:236-237. 8 GB: 4,052,022,880 + 810,404,576 = 4,862,427,456, which lib.rs:26-34 renders as `4.53 GB`. 16 GB: 7,661,641,408 + 1,532,328,281 = 9,193,969,689, rendered `8.56 GB`. claims.claim: The dispatching lead's four figures contradict the page.
claims.evidence: They do not. 4,052,022,880 / 1e9 = 4.05, / 2^30 = 3.77; 4,862,427,456 / 1e9 = 4.86, / 2^30 = 4.53; 7,661,641,408 / 1e9 = 7.66, / 2^30 = 7.14; 9,193,969,689 / 1e9 = 9.19, / 2^30 = 8.56. The lead's figures and the page's figures are the same four byte counts under two unit conventions, and the convention the product prints is the page's (crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:24-35, desktop-client/src/lib/probe.ts:158-164). Recorded as contradicted against the dispatch's premise, not against the page.

claims.claim: wiki/installing.md:96-97 describes four things downloading and unpacking at once, and that description of provisioning is accurate.
claims.evidence: desktop-client/src-tauri/src/provision.rs:1-14 describes three chains starting alongside the model download, the bundled backend, the inference engine and the Python runtime, then a fork to the voice model and the voice environment. The five rows are named at desktop-client/src/lib/probe.ts:120-134 as `The backend`, `Inference engine`, `Python runtime`, `Voice model`, `Voice engine`, and the chains are implemented at provision.rs:248-369.

claims.claim: The download figure printed beside that sentence covers only two of those items, because the inference engine and the Python runtime are fetched outside the planner.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:214-234 counts the model build and the voice weights and nothing else. The engine and the interpreter come from dictionary.yaml:28-36 and 37-54 and are fetched by desktop-client/src-tauri/src/provision.rs, chain B at 281-322 (dict.runtime.llama_server) and chain C at 324-369 (dict.runtime.python); their bytes never enter total_download_bytes. On macOS that is a further 11,040,494 (dictionary.yaml:46) plus 25,285,557 (dictionary.yaml:35), about 35 MB. On Windows with CUDA it is 250,727,763 plus 391,443,627 (dictionary.yaml:49, 51) plus 47,056,137 (dictionary.yaml:31), about 657 MB, before the voice environment's pip installs, which have no recorded size at all (dictionary.yaml:59-67). So the sentence and the number are both defensible in isolation and misleading beside each other.

claims.claim: The default install root on Windows is `D:\Hearth`, as wiki/installing.md:85-86 states.
claims.evidence: The page states it at wiki/installing.md:85-86. crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:232-237 states the opposite: on Windows the root is roomiest_non_system_drive() joined with `Hearth`, and that function at 256-272 filters out removable drives and the drive named by SystemDrive and then takes the one with the most free space. No drive letter appears anywhere in the file. When the machine has no such drive the function returns None and control falls through to lines 238-247, the visible `Hearth` in the user profile. The doc comment at 208-216 says the same in prose. `D:` is one possible outcome, never the default.

claims.claim: The hidden `.hearth` dotdir survives only on Linux.
claims.evidence: crates/hearth-probe/src/machine.rs:245-248: the visible `Hearth` is returned when the OS is macos or windows, and the `.hearth` dotdir is the return for everything else, with the comment at 239-244 recording that a dotdir on Windows was the bug. One caveat the page need not carry but the author should know: line 250 returns a bare relative `.hearth` on any platform when neither HOME nor USERPROFILE is set.

gaps: No page in the corpus states how many bytes the inference engine and the Python runtime add to an install. A reader who sizes their download from wiki/installing.md:72 under-counts by about 35 MB on macOS and about 657 MB on Windows with CUDA, and the voice environment's pip installs have no recorded size anywhere (dictionary.yaml:59-67).

No page and no source states a documentation unit policy. The product renders GiB under a `GB` label (crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:24-35), the corpus follows it, and nothing records that as a decision, so the next reader to check a figure against a decimal-GB calculator will file the same defect this task was dispatched to fix.
No page states which machines actually take turns between the mind and the voice. The corpus attributes it to an 8 GB Mac, which is wrong, and nothing states the VRAM band where it is right.

No canonical or primary source outside the repository exists for any of this. Hearth reaches no external service and publishes no vendor reference, so `source` is the highest authority available and every behavioural claim above rests on it.
open_questions: Should wiki/installing.md keep the product's unit convention, GiB printed under a GB label, or restate its figures in decimal GB? The four figures at lines 42-44, 72 and 75 are correct under the first and wrong under the second, and the same bytes produce the dispatching lead's 4.05, 4.86, 7.66 and 9.19. Matching what the installer prints on screen argues for keeping the page as it is; nothing in wiki/style-guide.md or wiki/page-types.md states a rule, and this run found no source that settles which convention the corpus should use.

Does T1 correct the sentence at wiki/installing.md:96-97 by narrowing it to the two items the plan's number counts, or by keeping all four and separating the number from the sentence? Both are true statements; the choice is the author's and this stage does not make it. Whichever is chosen has to be made consistently across wiki/clients/macos.md:51-54 and wiki/install-macos.md:84-86, which say the same thing.

Does the corpus want to state the provisioning bytes the plan figure omits, roughly 35 MB on macOS and 657 MB on Windows with CUDA? It is a real gap for a reader on a metered connection, but naming it is new content rather than a correction, and T1 is a corrections-only task per tasks/docs/tracker.md:309-311.

Is wiki/installing.md:100, `Every file is verified against a published sha256 hash once it lands`, T1's to fix or a new tracker row? It is contradicted by source, it sits inside the `## The download` section T1 already opens, and it is outside the task statement. This stage records the defect and does not decide the ownership.

Do wiki/backend/build-pipeline.md:106 and :158, wiki/backend/native-runtime.md:79, and wiki/features/second-brain.md:64 get tracker rows? All four are contradicted by source, all four carry defects T1 through T5 are correcting elsewhere, and none is owned by any task in tasks/docs/tracker.md. build-pipeline.md:158 in particular is a fourth instance of the coexistence claim.

Is the coexistence sentence at wiki/clients/windows.md:199-201, carried as an open question on T2, correct? This run derived that an 8 GB dedicated GPU plans tier 1 with the voice resident and does not take turns, and that the !coexist branch is reached at roughly 4.5 to 5.4 GB of VRAM. That is arithmetic from crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:110-159 and dictionary.yaml, not an executed planner run, and the page is T2's to settle, so it is passed on rather than answered.
notes:
TOOLS. Bash was available and used for all reading and searching (cat -n, sed -n, grep). I did not run cargo: the contract restricts Bash to search and read-only scripts, and building or running the probe is neither. Every planner figure below was therefore derived by hand from the formulas in crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs and the constants in crates/hearth-probe/dictionary.yaml rather than read off an executed run. The derivation validates against an independent point: it reproduces, exactly, the reason string the dispatching lead reported from a real run, `212 MB is left after the weights, which is about 17408 tokens of context at this model's rate`, including the 212 MB that only crates/hearth-probe/src/lib.rs:26-34 can produce from 221,861,383 bytes. I also did not run scripts/lint_wiki.py or scripts/doc_graph.py; neither bears on an affected-mode survey of one page, and no linter finding is in this artifact.

SIZE. S, unchanged from the dispatch but for different reasons than the dispatch gave. Three sentence-level corrections on one page in three sections: wiki/installing.md:76-78 (the contradiction), :85-86 (the Windows root), :96-97 (the four-things sentence). Not XS, because 76-78 needs a new true sentence rather than a substitution and the three sites are in three different sections. Not M, because it is one page and the four figure corrections the dispatch anticipated at lines 42-44, 72 and 75 turn out to be no-ops. THE HEADLINE, because the dispatch's premise on it is wrong.
